title: RAW UNREVIEWED: calibration carries one reference standard across distinct measured bodies
summary: A diagram/technical record may compare two bodies against the same explicit reference, yielding relations that are dimensionless rather than ingredient quantities or ordinal stages. The standard identity must be written and persist; image geometry supplies relative extent and orientation roles independently of numerals.
required_falsifier: Reject if R changes or is absent, if the proposed same standard needs a page-specific value, if image axes are ambiguous, or component order cannot distinguish measured body from reference without lexical repair.
exact_changed_research_decision: Determine whether a quantity-like paragraph supports shared-reference comparison rather than a count/recipe-stage account; no numerical interpretation or k/t polarity is assumed.

design.mechanism: Enter reference R and measured bodies A,B; COMPARE(A,R,axis) and COMPARE(B,R,axis) produce relational readings with the same fixed standard and axis. Directed composition preserves measured/reference role order, and wholeform differences account for parameter changes rather than arbitrary count glosses.
independent_constraints: Explicit shared standard and axis with no inferred universal unit.
Independently owned image extents/axes permit a relational comparison but do not select exact numeric values.
Exact-form dispersion, position and residuals fit reusable compare-argument syntax across both complete contexts.
